title: The spiral model and iterative development

videos.script: The waterfall assumes you can know everything at the start. The spiral assumes you cannot. {{assume}} So it goes round. Set objectives, find the biggest risk and reduce it, build and test, plan the next turn. Then again, a little larger. {{turns}} The second step is the heart of it. Each turn begins with one question. What is most likely to sink us, and what is the cheapest way to find out? {{risk}} At the cinema, that might be a paper seat map shown to five regulars, before a line of code exists. {{prototype}} Then two words people treat as one. Incremental means a piece at a time. Iterative means the whole thing, rough, then better. {{words}} And what building in turns does to testing. Every change can break what worked, so the checks for old work run again and again. {{regression}} That growing pile is regression testing, and it is why teams automate. {{end}}
